'''''Oenothera elata''''' is a species of ''[[Oenothera]]'' belonging to the family [[Onagraceae|'''Onagraceae,''']] known by the common name '''Hooker's evening primrose''' or '''tall evening primrose'''. Subspecies include ''hookeri'', ''hirsutissima'', ''longisima'', ''jamesii'', ''villosa'' and ''elata''.<ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 19 January 2018}}</ref> It is native to much of western and central North America. The plants are quite tall, especially the ''hookeri'' subspecies, native to [[California]], which can reach about 1.8 meters (6 feet) height.<ref name="Botanica 612">"Botanica. The Illustrated AZ of over 10000 garden plants and how to cultivate them", p. 612. Könemann, 2004. {{ISBN|3-8331-1253-0}}</ref>  The plants are found along roadsides, in moist meadows, or in woodland, from sea level up to {{convert|9000|ft|abbr=on}} in elevation.<ref name=ESierra>{{cite book|author=Laird R. Blackwell |title=Wildflowers of the Eastern Sierra and Adjoining Mojave Desert and Great Basin |year=2002 |publisher=Lone Pine Publishing |isbn=978-1-55105-281-6}}</ref>

==Description==
The stout, usually reddish stem has many long, narrow leaves, above a basal rosette. At its top is a large, open cluster of 2- to 4-inch wide yellow flowers with 4 large petals and protruding yellow stamens and 4-branched pistil, often covered in sticky pollen. The fragrant flowers open at dusk and wilt the next morning, turning orange or red.<ref name=ESierra/>

==Taxonomy==
''Oenothera elata'' was scientifically described and given its accepted name by [[Carl Sigismund Kunth]] in 1823.<ref name="POWO" /> It has {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]] of the species or one of its three subspecies according to [[Plants of the World Online]].<ref name="POWO" /><ref>{{cite POWO |id=77224437-1 |title=''Oenothera elata'' subsp. ==Uses==
The [[Zuni people]] apply a [[poultice]] of the powdered flower of the ''hookeri'' subspecies and saliva at night to swellings.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Camazine | first1 = Scott | last2 = Bye | first2 = Robert A. | year = 1980 | title = A Study Of The Medical Ethnobotany Of The Zuni Indians of New Mexico | journal = Journal of Ethnopharmacology | volume = 2 | issue = 4 | pages = 365–388 [377] | doi=10.1016/s0378-8741(80)81017-8 | pmid=6893476}}</ref>
